article_title: Learner Response System: Evaluation Report and Executive Summary
citation: Meg Wiggins, Mary Sawtell and Dr John Jerrim. (2017). Learner Response System: Evaluation report and executive summary. Education Endowment Foundation. https://www.educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk
title: LRS theory of change: instant two-way formative feedback improves pace and quality of feedback
description: The Edge Hill developers' logic model holds that timely, focused feedback facilitates learning: pupils respond to questions and are instantly told whether they erred, with suggestions for rectifying mistakes, while teachers receive aggregated feedback on each learner's progress, timing, attempts, and errors so they can adjust within the lesson and target struggling pupils. The report states "The LRS approach is based on the premise that timely and focused feedback is a powerful tool to facilitate learning". The trial tested this mechanism and found no measurable KS2 attainment benefit.
requirements: Teachers must become competent in using all key features of the system and deliver lessons using the handsets in at least three sessions a week, per the developers' logic model
An IT system that runs the software effectively, good ICT support at school level, and expert LRS support sufficient to help even the least confident teachers
constraints: The trial found no evidence of improved KS2 maths or reading results for either cohort, even in high-usage schools
Teachers and pupils noted the system could not let children show their working and occasionally gave negative feedback to wholly or partially correct answers
target_learners: Year 5 and Year 6 primary school pupils in England (aged 9-11), in schools with high proportions of pupils ever eligible for free school meals
target_learning_goals: Key Stage 2 maths and reading attainment
Improved pace and quality of classroom feedback and formative assessment
examples: Teachers used ad hoc and pre-prepared questions with aggregated results displayed on the whiteboard, and self-paced question sets with automatic differentiation and a results timeline showing who was getting questions right or wrong
